decisive_spans.text: When she smiles, the right lower lip deviates inward; frowning, forehead wrinkling, eye closure, and nasolabial fold depth are symmetric on both sides.

response.rationale: The vignette describes a child with asymmetric facial movement, specifically the right lower lip deviating inward when smiling or crying, while other facial movements are symmetric. This is the hallmark of Asymmetric crying face syndrome. Candidate D4, Congenital unilateral hypoplasia of the depressor anguli oris muscle, is a specific cause of this syndrome, but D1 is a broader and more direct description of the observed symptoms.
